title: Chain of command for Barbara
statementMd:
List Barbara Liskov's management chain: her manager, that manager's manager, and so on up to the top. Show first name and distance (1 = direct manager).

Expected columns: `first_name`, `dist`.

Tables: `employees`, `departments`.

**Row order matters** for this problem.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, manager_id, first_name, dist) AS (SELECT m.id, m.manager_id, m.first_name, 1 FROM employees b JOIN employees m ON m.id = b.manager_id WHERE b.first_name = 'Barbara' UNION ALL SELECT m.id, m.manager_id, m.first_name, c.dist + 1 FROM chain c JOIN employees m ON m.id = c.manager_id) SELECT first_name, dist FROM chain ORDER BY dist;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
